en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on the Puzzles, Section One: The Power of Supernormal Success (Iddhibalavagga)
10. The Question on the Vision of the Power of Supernormal Success “Venerable Nāgasena, this has been said by the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, the four bases of supernormal success have been developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, and made a foundation by the Tathāgata...’”
“Having been undertaken, developed, and well-undertaken, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could, if he so desired, remain for an eon or for the remainder of an eon.
Yet again it was said:
“After the passing of three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna.”
"If, venerable Nāgasena, it was said by the Blessed One:
'Ānanda, for the Tathāgata, the four bases of psychic power have been cultivated... [and so on] ...or for the remainder of a kappa,' then the limitation of three months must be wrong.
If, venerable sir, it was said by the Tathāgata—"

‘In three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain final nibbāna,’ then that statement—‘Ānanda, the four bases of psychic power have been developed by the Tathāgata... [as far as] for the remainder of an eon’—is likewise false.
There is no thundering by Tathāgatas out of place.
The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are speakers of unerring words, speakers of truth, speakers of non-dual words.

“This too is a double-edged question, profound, subtle, and difficult to contemplate, which has come before you. Tear asunder this web of views, settle it on one side, and refute the arguments of your opponents.

“Indeed, Great King, this was said by the Blessed One: ‘Ānanda, the four bases of psychic power have been developed by the Tathāgata... [omitted] ...or for the remainder of a kappa. And a three-month period was also mentioned; however, that ‘kappa’ is called a lifespan-kappa.”
"No, great king, the Blessed One did not say this while praising his own power; rather, great king, the Blessed One said this while describing the power of psychic potency (iddhi):
'Ānanda, the four bases of psychic potency have been developed by the Tathāgata... [and so on]... or for the remainder of the eon.
Great king, it is just as if a king had a noble steed, swift-moving with the speed of the wind, and the king [describes] its power of speed..."
Praising it in the midst of the people of the cities and the countryside, the army, the forces, the brahmins, the householders, and the ministers, he would say:
"Sirs, if this excellent horse so desires, it could traverse the earth bounded by the waters of the ocean and return here in an instant.
Yet he would not display that speed and gait to that assembly, even though such speed exists.
He would be capable of traversing in an instant the earth bounded by the waters of the ocean.

In the same way, Great King, the Blessed One, extolling his own power of psychic potency (*iddhibala*), spoke thus while seated in the midst of those possessed of the three knowledges (*tevijja*), the six direct knowledges (*chaḷabhiñña*), the arahants with taints destroyed and stainless, and among gods and humans:
"Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s four bases of psychic potency have been developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, and made a foundation."
“‘If it were developed, cultivated, and well-undertaken, then, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could, if he so desired, remain for an eon or for the remainder of an eon.
And that power of supernormal success (iddhibala) exists, Great King, in the Blessed One;

the Blessed One is capable of remaining for an eon or for the remainder of an eon by means of that power of supernormal success, yet the Blessed One does not display that power of supernormal success before that assembly.”
“Great King, the Blessed One has no need for any states of existence, and all states of existence are censured by the Tathāgata.
For this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, just as even a tiny amount of excrement is foul-smelling;’”
“In the same way, monks, I do not praise even a trifling existence, not even for as long as the snap of a finger.
“Great King, having seen all states of existence, destinies, and wombs as equal to excrement, would the Blessed One, by relying on his power of psychic potency,
still harbor desire and lust for those existences?”
“No indeed, venerable sir.
“In that case, Great King, it was while extolling the power of psychic potency that the Blessed One uttered such a lion’s roar of a Buddha,” said Nāgasena.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; thus do I accept it.”
The tenth question: On the Vision of the Power of Psychic Potency.
The first chapter: On the Power of Psychic Potency.
In this chapter there are ten questions.
